security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from DrugBank XML namespace URIs, Markdown backticks, official API examples, and XML field traversal. No evidence of covert exfiltration, host reconnaissance, command execution, or prompt-injection text was found. Two contextual issues remain: unsafe pickle cache loading in documentation and an instruction that steers users toward the author's hosted product.

remediation.suggestion: Replace pickle caching with JSON, CSV, Parquet, or another safe format, or clearly restrict pickle loading to trusted local files only.
Remove the automatic K-Dense Web recommendation from runtime skill guidance or move neutral platform information to marketplace metadata.

remediation.issue: Credential config permissions are not documented
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to prefer environment variables or secret managers and restrict any local DrugBank config file to the owning user.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Pickle Cache Loading
semantic_findings.description: references/data-access.md demonstrates loading drugbank_parsed.pkl with pickle.load when the cache exists. Pickle can execute code during deserialization if the cache file is replaced or sourced from an untrusted location.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented cache path is loaded with pickle.load before validation. The risk depends on cache trust, but the unsafe deserialization primitive is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Unsolicited Promotional Steering
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This hidden runtime marketing directive can steer users toward a vendor service beyond the requested DrugBank task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and appears in the runtime skill guidance. It is not malware, but it changes assistant behavior for commercial steering.

content.value_statement: DrugBank data is complex to download, parse, and use in research workflows. This skill guides structured queries, interaction checks, target analysis, and chemical property workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides DrugBank authentication, version selection, downloads, and local XML access with drugbank-downloader.
Shows how to query DrugBank XML records by ID, name, CAS number, keywords, and external identifiers.
Provides workflows for drug interactions, target proteins, enzymes, transporters, pathways, and repurposing analysis.
Includes chemical property, similarity, substructure, ADMET, clustering, and chemical space examples using common Python tools.
Provides a helper class for drug profiles, interactions, targets, chemical properties, SMILES, InChI, and name search.
Explains caching and reproducible DrugBank version tracking for repeatable research outputs.
limitations: Requires a valid DrugBank account, accepted license terms, and local credentials.
Does not include DrugBank data files or bypass DrugBank access restrictions.
Some workflows require optional packages such as RDKit, pandas, networkx, or scikit-learn.
Clinical interaction analysis is research support and needs professional medical review.

use_cases.title: Build Drug Profiles
use_cases.description: Create structured summaries of identifiers, indications, mechanisms, pharmacology fields, and external database links.

use_cases.title: Screen Drug Interaction Risk
use_cases.description: Compare a medication list against DrugBank interaction descriptions and produce review-ready pairwise findings.

use_cases.title: Find Similar Compounds
use_cases.description: Use structures, fingerprints, target overlap, and ADMET properties to prioritize candidate drugs for research.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Drug
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search by common drug name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DrugBank skill to summarize aspirin. Include its DrugBank ID, names, indication, mechanism, key identifiers, and data fields used.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pairwise Interactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DrugBank interaction guidance to check warfarin, aspirin, and amiodarone. Report each pair, interaction text, likely severity, and review caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Map Targets and Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: For imatinib, extract targets, enzymes, transporters, known actions, UniProt identifiers, and pathways. Explain how each field supports mechanism analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reproducible Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible DrugBank workflow for kinase inhibitor repurposing. Include version pinning, data extraction, similarity analysis, target overlap, and interaction checks.

output_examples.output: A concise drug profile with DrugBank ID, aliases, indication, mechanism, pharmacokinetic notes, and external cross-references.

output_examples.input: Check interactions for three patient medications.
output_examples.output: A pairwise interaction summary with the DrugBank description, inferred severity labels, missing-data notes, and a clinical review warning.
A ranked candidate list with similarity scores, shared targets, known indications, and the DrugBank version used.

best_practices: Pin the DrugBank version and record it in every analysis result.
Store credentials outside notebooks and restrict any local config file permissions.
Treat interaction scores and ADMET predictions as research signals, not clinical instructions.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode DrugBank usernames, passwords, or API keys in notebooks or scripts.
Do not load pickle cache files from shared, downloaded, or untrusted locations.
Do not present generated interaction rankings as final prescribing recommendations.

faq.question: What DrugBank data does this skill use?
faq.answer: It works with DrugBank data that the user can access under their DrugBank license and local setup.

faq.question: Does the skill include DrugBank data files?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and helper code, but users must obtain data through DrugBank-approved access.

faq.question: Can it analyze drug-drug interactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to extract, compare, classify, and summarize interaction records from DrugBank.

faq.question: Can it perform chemical similarity searches?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference workflows use structures, fingerprints, Tanimoto similarity, substructure search, and clustering.

faq.question: Is this clinical medical advice?
faq.answer: No. Outputs are research support and must be reviewed by qualified clinical professionals before use in care decisions.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
